v.rationale:
I ranked impl-2 first, impl-1 second and impl-3 third. All three test suites pass (impl-2: 30 tests, impl-3: 26, impl-1: 25), and the designs are close: commands defined with attributes, an ordered batch delete by id for the prune, and a ShouldBeUnique job with Tries(1), FailOnTimeout and UniqueFor under an hour, with retry_after raised to 3600. Two to four probes each confirmed that two schedule:run calls in the same minute push the job once and that cart batches are handled; for impl-2 and impl-1 they also confirmed the 03:00 prune fires exactly once on DST-change days and that the unique lock expires after a killed worker. impl-2's same-minute probe used the report email, which a Mail fake can't see because scheduled commands run in a separate process, so I checked the same behaviour on impl-3 and impl-1 with the job instead.

impl-2 ranks first. It applies Copenhagen time and onOneServer to every task in one group call, which I checked against the installed framework (v13.40). It bounds the overlap locks on both commands and has the strongest tests: the DST-change day, schedule:run integration, both boundaries, mail rendering and idempotency. Its only weakness is a tight 45-minute job timeout.

impl-1 ranks second. It is correct and uses local time consistently, with more timeout headroom than impl-2 and runInBackground on the prune. Its tests are thinner, though: one assertion is weak and there is no mail rendering test.

impl-3 ranks third because of its one real bug: the nightly prune has no timezone, so it runs at 02:00 UTC instead of Copenhagen time, unlike its other tasks. Its tests also have smells: unused imports, expect(true), asserting the raw cron string, and setTestNow instead of travelTo.
